# Kage source provenance

The eight archived source files are the exact text supplied by the user from
ThreeUI Pro. Their SHA-256 values, including final newlines, are in `manifest.json`.
This archive is outside the compiled Next.js source tree.

Canonical source: https://threeui.com/landing-pages/kage.html

The fourteen original WebP binary plates were retrieved from that page's asset
paths. Their local paths and SHA-256 values are in `binary-manifest.json`.
Runtime, embedded fonts and binary assets are under
`apps/web/public/landing-pages/secret-pathways-assets/`. The unchanged standalone
HTML is copied to `apps/web/public/landing-pages/kage-reference.html`.

The Pokémon adaptation is generated by
`apps/web/scripts/build-pokemon-journey.mjs` from the archived HTML plus the
`scene-parts/` landmark, runtime, markup and style fragments. It retains the exact
six camera stops, Catmull–Rom camera and target splines, ground-level forward
journey, final rise, atmosphere and giant wordmark animation. Landmarks and
lighting are adapted. The latest user-directed presentation replaces the source
text chapters and cloth image gallery with short headings and animated product
cards. The source cloth code remains archived but is not initialized by the
product presentation. No archived original source file is modified.

The current characters are rigged GLB models loaded by
`scene-parts/pokemon-characters.js.txt`, displayed by one shared renderer using
the original scene clock. Sources, hashes and asset-rights limitations are in
`vendor/pokemon-models/README.md`. No character PNG billboard is loaded. Previous-iteration
Pokédex artwork and its provenance remain under
`apps/web/public/landing-pages/pokemon-assets/artwork-sources.json`.

Output: `apps/web/public/landing-pages/pokemon-kage.html`.
React integration: `apps/web/src/components/dashboard/pokemon-world-hero.tsx`.
Handoff and verification: `docs/POKEMON_HERO_LOCAL_PREVIEW.md`.

This iteration is local only. No push or production release is authorized until
the user approves the visual result.
